paras: Abronia ornelasi, also known commonly as Ornelas's arboreal alligator lizard, the Cerro Baul alligator lizard,  and escorpión arboricola de Ornelas in Mexican Spanish, is a species of arboreal alligator lizard in the subfamily Gerrhonotinae of the family Anguidae. The species, which was originally described in 1984 by Jonathan A. Campbell, is native to southern Mexico.
The specific name, ornelasi, is in honor of Julio Ornelas Martinez who assisted Campbell in fieldwork in Mexico.
Abronia ornelasi is endemic to the Mexican state of Oaxaca.
The natural habitat of Abronia ornelasi is cloud forest at altitudes of 1,500–1,600 m (4,900–5,200 ft).
